new_upstream_defects: ThreadRuntime.swift:2890 and :2898 - spawnWaitingHeads removes a delegated task from hydraWaiting BEFORE attempting the spawn, then `guard let head = app.spawnDroppyHead(...) else { continue }` drops it with no note, no retry and no record. Because settleBatches only waits on the batch's pending set and on hydraWaiting (ThreadRuntime.swift:2611), the batch then settles without that head, the lead is handed the surviving reports and reports as though the whole block finished. Realistic worst outcome: a user delegates ten tasks, one spawn fails (no head slot resolvable, thread insert refused), and the work is silently never done while the chat says it is. upstream_defects.md entry 32 covers a DIFFERENT line of the same loop (:2889, the uncapped sweep when hydraLaunch is nil) and does not cover this. Recorded on PR-RUNTIME-233 as REPRODUCE, DO NOT FIX.

AppSettings.swift:363, :374 and the two sibling didSet blocks, with APIKeychain.swift:22-39 - when the Keychain refuses an API key write, the key is written to UserDefaults in plain text under deepseekAPIKey / metaAPIKey / zaiAPIKey / commandcodeAPIKey (AppSettings.swift:151-154), with nothing telling the user. Realistic worst outcome: a provider API key sits unencrypted in the app's defaults, readable by any process running as the user, on any machine where protected storage is unavailable. Not in upstream_defects.md. Recorded on the new PR-PROVREG-239.

AppSettings.swift:363 versus APIKeychain.swift:23 - the plaintext mirror is written UNTRIMMED from the input property while the Keychain stores the value trimmed of whitespace and newlines, so the two stores can hold different strings for the same key and a key pasted with trailing whitespace behaves differently depending on which store answered. Minor but observable. Not in upstream_defects.md. Recorded on PR-PROVREG-239.

AntigravitySession.swift:473 - the current-model test `currentID?.hasPrefix(parsed.baseSlug) == true` is not anchored on a separator, so a base slug that happens to be a prefix of an unrelated model id marks the wrong model as the default in the catalog. Realistic worst outcome: a new thread opens on a model the user did not choose. Not in upstream_defects.md. Recorded inside PR-PROVCLI-431 as upstream behaviour to reproduce, not fix.
consequential_candidates: Four third-party credential reads whose faithful reproduction would violate the port's own safety rules: PlanLimits.swift:181-211 (~/.claude/.credentials.json under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude, plus /usr/bin/security find-generic-password for the 'Claude Code-credentials' item), ProviderRegistry.swift:790-801 (~/.grok/auth.json), PiPlanLimits.swift:12-13 (Pi's <config>/auth.json) and CommandCodeAPI.swift:33-38 (~/.commandcode/auth.json). CLAUDE.md states 'Never read agent credential files' and names three of these paths explicitly. Concrete harm: the Windows build would read and, in the Pi case, TRANSMIT another agent's OAuth bearer token to api.anthropic.com and chatgpt.com usage endpoints - exposing a secret the app does not own to a third party over the network. I set all four to status DISCOVERED with an identical open_question naming the conflict, but the matching entry in unknowns.md and blocked_requirements.json could NOT be made because those two files are outside my editable set. One registered unknown covering all four still needs to be written by whoever owns the register, or Gate C will not fail on these paths.

PiPlanLimits.swift:27-34 additionally calls provider usage endpoints (https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, PiPlanLimits.swift:7-8) with that borrowed token. CLAUDE.md also forbids calling provider billing endpoints. Concrete harm: a network request carrying a third party's credential, attributable to the user's account, made without the user asking. Escalated on PR-PROVCLI-313 rather than reproduced.

AppSettings.swift:363 with APIKeychain.swift:39 - the plaintext API key mirror. Concrete harm: reproducing it faithfully writes a user's provider API key to disk unencrypted on every Windows PC where DPAPI is unavailable, which is exactly the fallback CLAUDE.md forbids ('If protected storage is unavailable, fail and say so; never fall back to plain text'). PR-PROVREG-239 is DISCOVERED with the decision left open; the clearing half of the rule (writing the empty string on a successful write) is safe and should be kept whatever is decided about the mirror.
